body: Any tradebacks with this change?

Performance should be exactly the same, though this could be verified with some benchmarking. The edges will be slightly more aliased than original solution, the screen will be less blurred. I tried to find a value that is a good balance between image quality and ghosting. It should be tested with various camera solutions (top-down, fps...), low and high-contrast scenes, moving geometry. So far I haven't found any issues in my various projects.

Perhaps we could consider changing it into a project settings parameter, This allows users to determine the historical frame blending weights according to their needs (higher weights might be effective for some dithering rendering features, while simply lowering this weight value may introduce some additional artifacts).

I think that's a good idea, but should be made as a separate PR.

@kubaofc123 Did you try a few values? 

I spent some time trying to understand where this comes from and it looks like it was originally described here: https://developer.download.nvidia.com/gameworks/events/GDC2016/msalvi_temporal_supersampling.pdf

At page 25 the author suggests using a value of 1. But later at page 32 suggest that anything between 0.75 and 1.25 appeared good to them. 

I found that slideshow while reviewing http://behindthepixels.io/assets/files/TemporalAA.pdf which suggests a value between 0.75 and 1.25. 

Personally, I wouldn't make the value configurable, but it would be good to test out a few values and confirm that either there isn't much difference within that range, or that we are happy with the tradeoffs. A lower value will lead to more aliasing, but less ghosting, while a higher value will lead to more ghosting.

Be advised, I'll be experimenting on changing the Clip History function, which throws out most of the current function, in order to resolve an Issue observed while developing my Game that's only present with TAA but not FSR 2/3 (Stars disappear when rotating camera) that has been linked to that function

This Seems to be because it's not doing what is advertised because the AABB it's clipping is a +/- avg of 9 colors and basically ditching a ton of important information and using an invalid mashup guess instead, instead of the min and max of those colors in 4D Chroma R, Chroma G, Chroma B and Brightness and clipping in that space.

This change will mean the history is going to be clamped between the lowest brightness and highest brightness of the Current Frame 3x3 kernel, and with the chroma range also being clamped to the min/max R, G and B values respectively

Reading the Linked Presentation I've realized that the Variance Clipping is using the wrong Velocity value.

Right now the Velocity being provided is the Closest Velocity in Depth.

However, Page 41-43 of the Presentation clearly states that you should use the Longest Velocity in the 3x3 kernel, not the one that's Closest in Depth in the 3x3 kernel (which is what TAA is currently using)

This is possibly related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104622 and nothing to do with the shader in which case enable physics interpolation, and disable it with `func _ready() -> void:
	get_tree().root.physics_interpolation_mode=Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF,` cap the framerate to physics tick rate, and ensure all queue_frees are deferred. This heavily reduces the occourance of this issue
